articleTitle: Integrating Zero Trust in the cyber supply chain security
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The cyber supply chain has been a target of sophisticated attacks. Vulnerabilities in components that were once considered secure due to perceived trusting relationships are being exploited. One way to reduce this type of cyber risk is through the use of a Zero Trust architecture. This type of approach revises trust in all relationships. It disregards the implicit trust in any component and is based on the premise of the existence of internal threats to the corporate network. The present work proposes to integrate a Zero Trust architecture in a cyber supply chain. The main contribution of this study is to propose an organization of security controls for a cyber supply chain in domains, enabling improvements in the security of the cyber supply chain by applying the principles of a Zero Trust architecture. The study also provides a checklist of controls that allows a gap analysis and suggests some ways of visualizing this result.

articleTitle: Computation of Transient Voltages on Wind Turbines on Frequency-Dependent Soil Caused by Lightning Strikes
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Wind energy is one of the main sources of renewable energy in power grids. In this context, wind turbines (WT) are subjected to lightning strikes due to their height and locations. In order to investigate the lightning performance of the WT, an equivalent circuit of the wind structure is implemented in the ATP software. For this analysis, the transient voltages on the WT located on frequency-dependent and -constant soils are calculated. First, the harmonic grounding impedance is computed for a frequency range from 100 Hz up to 5 MHz and the Ground Potential Rise (GPR) developed for the first and subsequent return strokes are assessed. Besides that, time-domain voltages along the WT generated by the same lightning currents injected at the tip of the blade are computed. Results indicated that the voltages at the injection point (blade) have no expressive impact for both soil models. Nevertheless, the GPR developed at the grounding system of the WT has a pronounced reduction for the high-resistive soil for both lightning currents. These results confirm the importance of considering the frequency-dependent soil in transient analysis.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation and Performance Evaluation of Multi-IRS Aided MIMO Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this paper, we study a channel estimation and joint beamforming design method for multi-IRS multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) systems. We consider a scenario where multiple intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) are located on the exact spot of the dominant channel scatterers. We investigate the spectral efficiency (SE), benefits and drawbacks of deploying multiple IRSs in comparison with a scenario with a single or no IRS. Our simulation results show a trade-off between the number of reflecting elements and the total number of IRSs in the system.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Signature based Implicit Object Movement Detection in an Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper considers implicit detection problem of object movement in an indoor environment. Specifically, based on radio frequency (RF) attributes in multicarrier transmissions, channel state information (CSI) is exploited to recognize the dynamics of monitoring area. Two wireless communication nodes in the room share the CSI as a byproduct, which fluctuates sensitively according to the movements of objects in the channel space. Thus, by tracking the changes of the CSI, movements of objects can be implicitly detected with simple statistical measures. To this end, we conduct experiments with universal software radio peripheral (USRP) settled onto linear stage in conditions where the object has different sizes and speeds. In numerical evaluation, we analyze the detection performance of the RF signature based implicit object movement detection under various experimental conditions. The results show that the proposed scheme effectively detects the movement of objects, even for small ones less than half of the RF wavelength.

articleTitle: Past, Present, and Future Trends of Traveling Wave-Based Fault Location Solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this paper, a literature review is carried out to highlight pioneer methods, recent promising proposals and future trends regarding traveling wave (TW)-based fault location (TWFL) solutions. The obtained results from a survey with Brazilian electrical engineers on TW-based applications are firstly analyzed, and then, different TWFL methods are qualitatively assessed, pointing out their advantages and shortcomings. Finally, based on these studies, a line of reasoning that explains some recent technological directions is identified, allowing to draw conclusions on potential trends for the coming years.

articleTitle: Preventing APT attacks on LAN networks with connected IoT devices using a zero trust based security model
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Many organizations are being targeted by different types of attacks. One of the most dangerous attacks is called Advanced Persitent Threats (APT) as it is silent and focused on espionage and information theft, unlike a denial of service (DoS) attack. The proposed solution addresses the implementation of a security model based on zero trust in order to prevent APT attacks on LAN networks. The proposal is to use the concepts of micro-segmentation and Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs). Many IoT devices are present in most networks and most of them have several vulnerabilities that can facilitate the theft of information and compromise the local network.

articleTitle: RF SP4T FET Switch at Ku-band for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The presented paper shows the design of a microwave switch operating between 11.7GHz and 12.2GHz (Ku-band) that is a part of a transceiver for a mobile satellite communication system. Different from other switches with PIN diodes and more power capability, this specific switch uses JFET transistors for low consumption, low noise, low insertion loss, low return loss, and high insulation. It was developed to be manufactured in microstrip, making possible a large-scale production. Its simulation results demonstrate good aspects, and it is ready for the next step, fabrication, and testing.

articleTitle: Practical Hardware Models and Beamforming Design for IRS-Assisted MIMO Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has emerged as a promising technology to enhance wireless communications by smartly shaping the radio propagation environment. In this paper, we integrate the IRS to a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless network via the joint design of the IRS reflecting coefficients and the transmit beamforming at the base station (BS) and user equipment (UE) to enhance the spectral efficiency. We evaluate the impact of different optimization solutions to enhance spectral efficiency considering the hardware model of the IRS. Simulation results indicate that the IRS successfully enhances the performance of the wireless network in terms of spectral efficiency even when the degradation due to realistic hardware models is considered.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of Isolated Modular Hydrokinetic Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper assesses the performance of renewable energy generation systems based on hydrokinetic turbines and permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSG). For this purpose, in each unit the turbine is modeled through its power curve and the PMSG model is based the well-known dq-frame reference approach. The electronic interface with the load is composed of a boost converter, used for maximum power point tracking (MPPT), and a buck converter for DC bus voltage stabilization. An electric power generation system is then composed by three hydrokinetic generators and its behavior is tested for variable load and river speed. The results demonstrate that these systems can provide support for electric energy generation with high efficiency, keeping constant the load voltage. Also, it is possible to confirm that the parallel operation of these units at different points of a river can be realized due to control systems. Finally, the simulation allows to visualize that normal operation of generation units can be maintained even when one of them operates without the MPPT algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Two-Level and Modular Multilevel Converters in High Voltage Direct Current Systems Under Fault Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: Victor R. F. B. de Souza

abstract: The occurrence of faults in multi-terminal high voltage direct current (MTDC) systems is a critical situation for both control and protection systems. For instance, MTDC systems work under large overcurrents during DC faults due to the discharging of capacitors on the DC side and the feeding of AC fault current to the DC system via the converters’ anti-parallel freewheeling diodes, challenging their operation, control, and protection. Therefore, the behavior analysis of MTDC systems based on modular multi-level converter (MMC) when submitted to a critical situation is essential to develop fast and accurate protection systems and control strategies. The main goal of this paper is to present a comparison between a six-level MMC (6L-MMC) and a two-level voltage source converter (2L-VSC) for MTDC systems under DC and AC faults to highlight the main challenges for the control and protection systems, such as DC fault blocking capability, integration of AC and DC systems during different operating conditions, fault propagation, and DC voltage control.

Author Keywords: Multi- Terminal High Voltage Direct Current

articleTitle: Source Extraction based on Binary Masking and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this article we present a study of a different approach to the source separation problem, exploring neural networks to extract a target speech from a noisy mixture. The solution consider time-frequency representations of the signal, to which a mask is applied in order to recover the desired signal. Simulation results indicate that the approach is able to attain a performance similar to the ideal mask, designed with full knowledge about the desired signal.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Energy Losses Using Smart Meter Data
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The evaluation of technical and non-technical losses is essential for utilities due to their impacts on the efficiency of the systems, energy tariffs, and utility revenue. To reduce the losses, many utilities are supporting the installation of smart meters. This paper presents a real case of application of smart metering data for evaluation of energy loss in low voltage distribution systems. This evaluation relies on real measurements from distribution transformers and customer smart meters. Inaccurate and missing data in measurement and network databases are among the main challenges faced to accomplish this task.

articleTitle: Technical Feasibility Study of the Current Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor Technology in a Zigbee Transceiver Design
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The present work demonstrates the realization of a technical feasibility study in the use of transistors with carbon nanotubes (CNTFets) using the purity level currently possible. With this in mind, a Zigbee transceiver was designed, containing the upconversion and downconversion mixers developed with CNTFets. The circuit performance was then compared with that obtained with similar circuits designed with CMOS transistors. It was possible to verify a better linearity and lower power consumption of circuits designed with CNTFets. The CNTFets were simulated with the CCAM model (Compact Carbon Nanotube Field-Effect Transistor Model), developed by the University of Dresden using the Verilog-A language.

articleTitle: NERD: a Network Exfiltration Rootkit Detector based on a Multi-agent Artificial Immune System
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The expansion of the Internet has also seen a great increase in cyber threats. Among the main threats seen in this new scenario are Advanced Persistent Threats(APT’s) characterized by slow progress, high stealthiness and high impact. One of the tools used by cyber actors to allow the extended presence necessary to APT’s campaigns are rootkits, malware designed to subvert the Operating System allowing for processes, files and network traffic to be hidden from system administrators, and to allow easy access after the initial infection, which are extremely hard to detect. Marques et al. [1] have proposed the MADEX architecture, an Artificial Immune System (AIS) for flow analysis, that detects rootkits obfuscating network traffic. This work enhances the MADEX architecture so that it could handle more load without impact to its detection capabilities. This resulted in NERD, which can handle loads above those of the original MADEX with an improved accuracy of 99.996% and false positive rates below 0.08%.

articleTitle: Transient Responses on Transmission Lines Located Above Frequency-Dependent Soil with Variable Water Content
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of frequency-dependent soil parameters with variable water content in the transient responses of single-circuit three-phase transmission line (TL) subjected to lightning subsequent return stroke. For this purpose, we use the Nakagawa’s approach to compute the ground-return impedance and admittance matrices the frequency-dependent soil modeled by Messier is employed. With the Nakagawa’s approach, four water contents of 0.90%, 2.57%, 4.04% and 11.57% are selected with results in low-frequency resistivity of 5000, 1000, 500 and 100 Ω.m. The transient responses for single-circuit three-phase line located above soils of 100, 500, 1000, and 5000 Ω.m considering the frequency-constant soil using the Carson’s approach are compare. Results demonstrated that the inclusion of frequency dependence of soil leads to an expressive reduction of approximately 19.52% and 60.16% in the generated voltage peaks (first and third) for this TL located above a high-resistive soil of 5000 Ω.m and lower water content W = 0.90%. This work shows the impact of the frequency-dependent soil that must be taken into account for adequate transient in power systems.

articleTitle: Computational Impacts of Freezing the Jacobian Matrix in the HKW Method for Power Flow Applied to Ill-Conditioned Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The study of power flow in ill-conditioned power systems is still a challenge for most robust methodologies available, since they are not computationally competitive for wide use in industrial applications. Consequently, this paper aims to contribute in this theme by evaluating two approaches to solve the power flow problem inspired by the Heun-King-Werner (HKW) method of the Newton-Continuous philosophy. The original technique is modified in the sense that we propose to avoid the computation of all Jacobian matrices required along the iterative process. The HKW original method assumes the determination and LU factorization of two Jacobian matrices per iteration to obtain the PFP solution. This burden corresponds to an additional overhead computational compared to the standard Newton Raphson’s method. Thus, in this work, two approaches based on the freezing of the Jacobian matrix for the HKW method were proposed. Experiments considering six ill-conditioned large-scale power system models, including one with more than 70,000 buses are used to validate the proposed approaches. The classical Newton-Raphson method were used with the full HKW method to evaluate the performance of the proposed approaches. In all studied cases, results obtained with the developed approaches were promising, outperforming the original methodology.

articleTitle: On the Effects of EMI and the Soil Structure on Transmission Line Parameters — Part II: Impacts on Fault Locators
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for computing the electrical parameters of overhead transmission lines accounting for metallic pipeline interferences and soil stratification effects. The method is based on the closed-form analytical solution of the Carson’s integral, which is used to calculate self and mutual line parameters. The Alternative Transients Program (ATP) is used to simulate six short-circuit scenarios on a 60 Hz, 230 kV transmission line 200 km long, considering a hypothetical case of interferences with a pipeline and soil stratification based on resistivity measurements. Results show that zero sequence impedances are affected significantly due to the presence of the interfering structure, yielding errors of about 13% in phase-to-ground fault locations.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Weightless Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In the last few years, the demand for cloud-based high-performance systems has gone hand in hand with the field of Machine Learning (ML), as most deep learning models are increasingly requiring more powerful machines to efficiently handle soaring amounts of data on a daily basis. Although this seems like a good distributed solution, it actually leads to centralizing training and inference in commercially available data centers. Thus, this work presents a collaborative architecture that uses Weightless Neural Networks (WNNs) to enable concurrent training/inference in modern container-based cloud systems, such as Kubernetes and Docker Swarm. A WNN is a class of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) that uses a set of Random Access Memories (RAMs) to map training and classification information. Performance results show that our collaborative architecture can efficiently learn and classify well-know datasets in about 2 times faster than traditional architectures, while also being able to scale to many concurrent clients.

articleTitle: ADS-B Vulnerabilities Test Platform
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast System (ADS-B) is a technology that provides aircraft information for air traffic control systems. ADS-B provides several benefits to the airline industry such as higher accuracy of surveillance information, improved situational awareness of air traffic controllers and pilots and lower implementation costs when compared to traditional radars. Despite these advantages, ADS-B broadcasts unencrypted aircraft data over the air making it easy to decode, replicate or interfere with airline information. This article aims to expose three ADS-B vulnerabilities: spoofing, message repetition and message manipulation. A low-cost platform is proposed and demonstrated in order to enable security verifications related to ADS-B.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Noise Amplifier for Through-The-Earth Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The communication adopted in mining must reach its full extent, so that in the event of a disaster, the rescue of victims is efficient. Thus, the operationalization of an emergency communication system becomes necessary, and the Though-the-Earth (TTE) type of communication is an interesting candidate. Therefore, the focus of this work will be the development of a low noise amplifier that will integrate a receiver for TTE communication, where all blocks were designed using TSMC 0.18 μm technology. After the design and simulation stage, satisfactory results were found for the main amplifier, the folded cascode, with a gain of 73 dB, input-referred noise of $105.39\, \text{nV} /\sqrt {\text{Hz}}$ at 1.15 kHz and power consumption of 196 μW.

articleTitle: Analysis of Source and Load-side High Impedance Faults Using Stockwell Transform
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: High Impedance Faults (HIFs) occur due to the contact between an energized conductor and a high impedance surface. Because of the low amplitude fault current value and its random characteristics, there is no fully efficient solution for its detection. The vast majority of existing detection methods study only source side HIFs. To fill this gap, this paper analyzes the load side HIFs by using the current harmonic content, measured at the system substation, applying Stockwell Transform. The HIF is simulated through an impedance model using actual signals. The results reveal that low-frequency harmonics can be identified regardless of the fault location, mainly on the neutral than on the phase current. These conclusions can help researchers develop new methods to identify HIFs regardless of the scenario.

articleTitle: Time-Domain-Based Relay Model to Assess Line Protection Nearby HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The HVDC technology has driven the attention of power systems protection researchers to its impacts over protective schemes of AC transmission lines (TL) connected in the near vicinity of line-commutated converters (LCC). In the literature, it is reported that phasor estimation processes used in traditional protection schemes can lead its functions to misoperate when the commutation failure (CF) phenomena occur. In contrast, reports on the operation of time-domain protection schemes under the mentioned conditions are scarce. In this context, the study could have been carried out via an actual relay, but this does not provide the performance of the internal variables in order to allow a complete understanding of its operation. Therefore, in this paper, a time-domain-based relay model developed in the Alternative Transients Program (ATP) environment, is presented and applied in an AC TL, connected next to an LCC-HVDC link, to assess the performance of two time-domain protective schemes, TD32 and TD21, under CF scenarios allowing analysis of its internal operating quantities. As result, it is shown that despite the distortions caused by the CF in the voltage and current waveforms, the time-domain functions work reliably and fast, but some recommendations should be considered.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Analysis of DG Anti-Islanding Protection Security Against Momentary Short-Circuits in Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The islanding protection schemes are used to disconnect distributed generators as soon as possible when an islanding event occurs. Moreover, the protection needs to be secure and not act for events other than islanding, such as short-circuit, load switching or normal fluctuations in the grid voltage and frequency. Recent events have raised concerns about the safety of the protection scheme and the IEEE 1547-2018 standard established ride-through requirements, presenting recommendations about the disconnection of distributed generators in case of excursions of the system’s electrical quantities. Therefore, this paper presents a probabilistic analysis of frequency, rate of change of frequency and fast rate of change of frequency protection security in the occurrence of momentary short-circuit events in the distribution system. The results have shown that the risk of undesired operation is significant, but adopting strategies such as time delay settings and undervoltage block function, the global risk can be reduced from 98.78% to 4.51%, considering the simultaneous operation of the three passive techniques.

articleTitle: Solid waste management and monitoring system for smart cities: development of a low-cost sustainable IoT architecture using GPRS/GSM
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: Pedro de O. Moura e Souza
Gustavo P. C. P. da Luz

abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are getting more common every day and being used by a diversity of applications, such as health, wearables, and smart cities. Nonetheless, there is a gap between energy-saving and data transfer capacity from the sensors to great distances, using IP networks. Proposals such as narrowband are promising, however, there is not as much coverage into big centers as 2G technology has. This work proposes the development of a solution to monitor smart containers, using solar plate-powered devices and sending collected data using 2G mobile networks, without needing to recharge the battery manually from the devices, with high energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Student Dropout Prediction in MOOC using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Students’ high dropout rate is a common problem on Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) platforms. Therefore, minimizing this problem requires identifying as soon as possible students who have a high probability of dropping out of the course. In this paper, we propose an approach to predict student dropout in the Virtual School of Government (EV.G), elaborating a model that can predict the students’ situation at the end of the course based on their performance in the first days and information about their access to the online platform. The processing of the data used was performed with subsequent application of automatic learning techniques, using historical data from EV.G.

articleTitle: A Review on Techniques to Increase Hosting Capacity of Distribution Systems to DERs
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a structured literature review regarding techniques to increase the hosting capacity of distribution systems to distributed energy resources. The structured search with some filtering criteria was done using the IEEE Xplore<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> and Scopus<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> databases. The review has identified that the techniques range from traditional practices (e.g., network reinforcement and reconfiguration, installation of voltage regulators, etc.) to the more advanced ones (e.g., adoption of soft open points, energy storage systems, smart inverter control capabilities, etc.). Moreover, the paper summarizes essential insights regarding the main techniques.

articleTitle: Hybrid Architecture for Intrusion Prevention and Detection in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This year the number of IoT devices has already surpassed 8 billion. However, the focus of these embedded devices is to provide the proposed services without worrying about their security. This article proposes a Host Intrusion Detection and Prevention System (HIDPS) for hybrid architectures, identifying security flaws and preventing attacks using the computational paradigm FoG computing. The decentralized communication used in this solution takes place through the use of a technology similar to a Blockchain, the Tangle, thus allowing for greater reliability of the entire solution.

articleTitle: On the Effects of EMI and the Soil Structure on Transmission Line Parameters — Part I: Theoretical Model
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for computing the electrical parameters of overhead transmission lines accounting for metallic pipeline interferences and soil stratification effects. The method is based on the closed-form analytical solution of the Carson’s integral, which is used to calculate self and mutual line parameters. Obtained results reveal that zero sequence impedances may be significantly affected by uncertainties due to metallic pipeline interferences and soil layered structure, thereby a more robust line parameter calculation in practical applications is required to avoid errors in line design which uses zero sequence as fundamental parameters. In a companion paper, the methods developed discussed in this part are employed to evaluate a wide variety of fault scenarios on a 230 kV transmission line 200 km long, 60 Hz, considering a hypothetical case of interferences with a metallic pipeline and soil stratification based on resistivity measurements.

articleTitle: Techno-economic assessment of photovoltaic plants with and without tracking systems in Brazil
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Developing countries with high values of irradiation, such as Brazil, tend to seek photovoltaic generation systems as a solution to meet the growing demand for electricity from a clean and renewable source. However, the slight capacity factor of these systems is often an obstacle. Solar tracking is used to improve the performance of photovoltaic systems, although the installation cost of photovoltaic systems with this gadget and its maintenance is higher. Considering this scenario, this study aims to analyze the feasibility of implementing a 20 MW photovoltaic plant with and without tracking in the five regions of Brazil under the technical and economic aspects. For this, deterministic techniques of investment evaluation are used in the Brazilian regulatory scenario, and computer simulations and univariate sensitivity analysis are performed for the parameter that most impact economic viability, exchange rate. The results of this article show that the single-axis system presented the best economic performance for most regions. The analysis conducted contributes to efficient decision-making regarding the process of improvement of the Brazilian energy matrix.

articleTitle: Investigation Study on the Voltage Stability Status of a Power Flow Problem Solution
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation study to verify the voltage stability status for a power flow problem solution. After solving the power flow problem (PFP) by the Newton-Raphson (NR) method, the voltage stability problem is evaluated. The voltage stability analysis employs classical techniques based on Q-V curves, V-Q sensitivities and modal analysis. The main purpose is to evaluate the voltage stability associated to the system operation point and identify possible instability related sites which causes this problem. In order to illustrate the importance of the study, experiments are carried out by using a 6-, 118-, 300-, 2746- and 9241-bus system. Some of these systems show clear instability voltage problems, which are associated to unstable figures. Results in terms of Q-V curves, V-Q sensitivities, computation of eigenvalues and participation factors are important figures obtained to evaluate the voltage stability status of the system operation point. This aspect can be useful since it provides a tool to determine an adequate reactive support for a specific studied system.

articleTitle: Organizers
publicationTitle: 2021 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members and society officers.
